the default time of a firm is a totally inaccessible stopping time in the filtration of the market and that default probabilities are increasing in the state variable.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a generalization of structural models of defaultable assets, where the default is driven by a latent process, which can be correlated with the market.

we show that the market’s information is insufficient to determine the default time and that the default intensity process cannot be recovered from observable market prices, even though the default time can be identified.
the credit spread is the difference between the expected payoff and the expected value of the discounted payoff.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the credit spread is not a function of the default probability alone but depends also on the volatility of the state variable.
in the absence of information on the state variable driving default, the default probability and hence the credit spread are increasing with respect to the price process.

, even if investors cannot observe the default trigger variable directly, they can still extract useful information from the observed price process, which allows them to infer the default probabilities and to value the default-sensitive securities.
